Texas City oil and gas NDT training: the direct answer

For Texas City, oil and gas NDT training means ASNT SNT-TC-1A coursework in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, aimed at the large refinery process units and chemical plants on Galveston Bay. Atlantis NDT delivers it live online or onsite at your Texas City facility, with ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice. Radiographers also need Texas DSHS certification. Atlantis has no Texas City training centre.

Texas City is a compact market with very large equipment. A few refining and chemical complexes share the bayfront, and their process units (crude, cokers, hydrotreaters, reformers, alkylation) run on long inspection cycles that end in big, tightly planned turnarounds. This page covers what that means for training: heavier advanced UT, process-safety expectations, coastal corrosion, and the paperwork owners check.

Oil and gas NDT work in Texas City

Marathon Petroleum's Galveston Bay Refinery in Texas City is among the largest refining complexes in the United States. It was formed when Marathon combined its original Texas City refinery with the former BP site it bought in 2013. Valero operates a second refinery on the east side of the industrial area, and chemical producers including Eastman have plants nearby. The Port of Texas City handles liquid bulk through its docks and pipelines. We name these facilities as context only. None is presented as an Atlantis client.

Texas City also carries a process-safety history that still shapes how inspection is done. The 2005 explosion at the isomerization unit of what was then the BP Texas City refinery was investigated by the US Chemical Safety Board, and its findings changed how the industry thinks about process safety culture and mechanical integrity. For NDT technicians the practical consequence is simple: owners here expect rigorous procedures, traceable data and personnel records that would stand up to an incident investigation.

The work that follows from that profile includes:

  • Heavy-wall vessels and reactors. Hydroprocessing reactors, separators and coke drums have thick walls and demanding weld examinations. Turnarounds bring PAUT and TOFD for weld examination and flaw sizing.
  • Damage mechanism screening. Units in hot hydrogen service are assessed for high temperature hydrogen attack under API RP 941. Advanced UT techniques are used to look for it, and they need highly trained Level II and Level III operators. Coke drums, sulfuric and hydrofluoric acid alkylation units, and sour water systems each have their own mechanisms to check.
  • Coastal and atmospheric corrosion. Salt air from Galveston Bay drives external corrosion, corrosion under insulation and pipe-support corrosion across the site. UT thickness programmes and VT of supports are constant work.
  • Storm recovery. After a Gulf hurricane or flood, owners often need large volumes of VT and UT condition checks before units restart.

Methods mapped to Texas City process units

MethodTexas City oil and gas applicationCode or standard (context)
PAUTWeld examination on reactor, vessel and piping repairs; corrosion mapping on drums and shells; some damage-mechanism screening techniquesASME Section V Article 4; owner advanced-UT procedures
TOFDFlaw detection and through-wall sizing in heavy-wall welds, often combined with PAUTASME Section V Article 4 and mandatory appendices
UT (thickness and shear wave)CML surveys on refinery piping circuits; shear-wave weld work on repairs and tie-insOwner API 570 and 510 programmes; ASME Section V
RTPiping tie-ins, small-bore welds and profile radiography for corrosion during turnaroundsASME Section V Article 2; B31.3; Texas DSHS radiation rules
MT (including wet fluorescent)Crack detection on carbon-steel welds in wet H2S, amine and caustic serviceASME Section V Article 7
PTStainless and alloy welds, including clad and overlay surfacesASME Section V Article 6
VTInternal vessel entries at turnaround; external condition, supports and storm-damage surveysASME Section V Article 9; owner inspection plans
ETExchanger tube bundles in the turnaround scopeASME Section V Article 8

Method spotlight for Texas City: PAUT and TOFD on heavy-wall welds. Texas City turnarounds involve thick, high-consequence equipment, and owners increasingly replace or supplement radiography with encoded ultrasonic examination. A technician who can calibrate on the right reference block, plan scans for full volumetric coverage, separate geometric indications from real ones, and size indications defensibly is worth far more to a Texas City contractor than one who can only take spot thickness readings. Our phased array training and TOFD training course are the core here, built on solid UT Level II fundamentals. Damage-mechanism screening techniques such as those used for HTHA are usually qualified by the owner or the technique provider. We teach the UT foundation and are honest that owner-specific technique qualification is a separate step.

From trainee to certified technician in Texas City

  1. Join an employer that certifies. SNT-TC-1A is an employer-based system. A refinery contractor or in-house inspection group sponsors your certification.
  2. Work to its written practice. The written practice sets hours, exams and recertification rules for each method and level. Companies that need one written or updated can use written practice development.
  3. Complete formal training in theory, technique, codes and safety. Check minimum hours on the training requirements matrix.
  4. Build documented experience. Turnaround work builds hours quickly, but each hour has to be logged and verified.
  5. Pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III. The specific exam should cover the owner procedures you will actually use.
  6. Clear the vision requirements: near-vision acuity and colour contrast, with the near-vision check renewed annually.
  7. Get certified by the employer, then recertify on the written-practice cycle. For advanced UT, expect owner performance demonstrations as an extra step.

A typical progression on the bayfront runs like this. A new hire starts on thickness surveys and VT. They add MT and PT for turnaround weld work. Then they move into shear-wave UT and, with enough experience, into encoded PAUT and TOFD, where advanced UT technicians spend much of each outage. Each step needs its own training, experience and exams under the written practice. Planning the sequence early lets a Texas City contractor have the next group of advanced UT technicians ready before the next major outage, instead of competing with every other contractor for the same few people.

Background reading: the SNT-TC-1A certification guide and the Level II path.

Process safety and mechanical integrity: why records matter in Texas City

Refineries and many chemical plants fall under OSHA's Process Safety Management standard, 29 CFR 1910.119. Its mechanical integrity element requires written procedures, inspection and testing that follow recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, and training for employees involved in maintaining process equipment. Contractors working on covered processes are expected to have trained, qualified people too. Owners meet those obligations partly by auditing the NDT contractors they hire.

In Texas City that means a contractor's certification files are not a formality. Expect owners to ask for the written practice, each technician's training and experience records, exam papers and grades, and current vision tests. Training that produces clean, auditable records is as valuable here as training that improves technique. Every Atlantis cohort includes graded exams and hour records formatted for certification files.

Radiography licensing, TWIC and site access in Texas City

As in the rest of Texas, industrial radiography in Texas City falls under the Texas DSHS Radiation Control program, operating under the state's NRC Agreement State status and 25 TAC §289.255. Nobody may act as a radiographer without a valid state radiographer certification. Candidates complete a qualifying radiation-safety course and work as radiographer trainees under a radiographer trainer before they apply. The certification ID card lasts five years. Check DSHS for current details.

That certification is a legal permission to work with sources. It is not the same as SNT-TC-1A RT certification, which covers technique and interpretation. Texas City contractors usually run the two in parallel for new radiographers. During large turnarounds, radiography is also tightly coordinated with operations to manage exclusion zones around crowded units, so site-specific radiation-safety briefings are common.

The Port of Texas City and the dock facilities serving the refineries are covered by maritime security rules, so TWIC is usually needed for unescorted access to those areas. Refinery badging also requires a contractor safety orientation, often the Houston Area Safety Council's Basic Orientation Plus, plus site-specific training.

Training delivery for Texas City teams

  • Live online for theory, code study and procedure reviews, including evening sessions for crews coming off day shift. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. We bring the instructor to your contractor yard or plant training room in Texas City, La Marque or the wider Galveston County area, and run practicals on your instruments, scanners and reference blocks.
  • Pre-turnaround bootcamps. These are focused blocks before a major outage that bring new Level IIs up to speed on PAUT and TOFD setups, owner procedures and reporting formats.

Texas City turnarounds are planned well ahead, so training should be too. Share your turnaround schedule and we will build a Texas City training plan around it.

Level III services for Texas City contractors

Advanced UT work increases the load on a company's Level III: technique sheets, scan plans, data review and exam administration. Atlantis supports Texas City employers with:

  • Written practice revisions that properly cover PAUT and TOFD as techniques under UT.
  • Practical exams on real flawed specimens for advanced UT candidates.
  • Procedure and technique review against ASME Section V and owner specifications.
  • Level III support during audit preparation.

Plant-owner work is covered on NDT consulting in Texas City and refining NDT consulting in Texas City. Group programmes are on corporate NDT training. Book a Level III consultation for your Texas City team.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator offers 12 methods across 5 environments, including an oil and gas site and an NDT lab. Texas City trainees can use it to rehearse scan planning, probe placement and indication recognition before hands-on sessions. It is a practice tool only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens, and it does not count toward experience hours.

Your instructor

Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, leads the training and Level III work. Senior technicians can use our ASNT Level III exam preparation.

NDT training options for Texas City, compared

  • San Jacinto College. Its Inspection Technologies programme, with NDT and fixed-equipment inspection tracks, is the closest college NDT programme, a drive up State Highway 146. Confirm schedules with the college.
  • College of the Mainland. The Texas City community college is known for process and industrial programmes. Check with it directly whether any NDT coursework is currently offered; we could not confirm a dedicated NDT programme.
  • Houston-area NDT schools. Several established schools offer open-enrolment classroom courses within commuting distance.
  • Contractor in-house programmes. Refinery inspection contractors train many of their own technicians.
  • Atlantis NDT. We fit employers that want advanced-UT-heavy cohorts trained to their own written practice, onsite or live online, with Level III exams and audit-ready records. We are not a walk-in school.

Texas City oil and gas NDT training: FAQ

Where can I get oil and gas NDT training near Texas City?

Options include San Jacinto College's NDT programme, Houston-area schools, contractor in-house training, and employer-arranged training from Atlantis, delivered live online or onsite at a Texas City facility. Atlantis has no physical location in Texas City.

Which NDT skills do Texas City refineries need most?

UT thickness work is constant. Turnarounds add strong demand for PAUT and TOFD on heavy-wall welds, MT in wet H2S and caustic service, RT on tie-ins, and ET on exchanger bundles.

Is PAUT training enough to work on HTHA inspections?

Not on its own. HTHA screening uses specialised advanced UT techniques that owners or technique providers usually qualify separately. Strong UT and PAUT fundamentals are the prerequisite.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Texas City?

Yes. A Texas DSHS radiographer certification under 25 TAC §289.255 is required to act as a radiographer, and your employer must hold the right radiation licence or registration. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is separate.

Can I take NDT classes online in Texas?

Yes, for the classroom portion. Practical exams and on-the-job experience still need hands-on work.

How long does it take to become a UT Level II in Texas City?

That depends on your employer's written practice and prior experience. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum hours that employers may adjust with justification. See the training requirements matrix and practise with our UT Level 2 practice questions.

Will Atlantis training make me an API inspector?

No. API 510, 570 and 653, and API's QUTE and QUPA, are API certifications with their own requirements. We train NDT technicians to SNT-TC-1A.

What does oil and gas NDT training in Texas City cost?

We quote on request, based on methods, levels, number of technicians, delivery format and any exam or written-practice work. Cohort and onsite quotes are usually returned within one business day. Request a Texas City training quote.

Can WIOA or the GI Bill pay for NDT training?

Only at approved providers. Texas WIOA funding goes through local Workforce Solutions boards and their eligible provider lists, and GI Bill benefits need a VA-approved programme. Atlantis does not claim those approvals. Employer-paid training is the usual route for refinery contractors.

Do I need TWIC to work in Texas City?

For dock and port areas covered by maritime security rules, yes, for unescorted access. Refineries also require contractor safety orientation and site-specific training.

Can you run a pre-turnaround PAUT course at our Texas City yard?

Yes. Onsite cohorts on your own scanners and reference blocks are a core Atlantis service. Ask about onsite advanced UT training in Texas City.

What do NDT technicians earn around Texas City?

Earnings depend on method, level, overtime and turnaround work. We do not publish unsourced local numbers; our NDT salary guide covers published ranges.
